rv.q: Mr. Leveaux's ''Nine'' isn't big on momentum or coherence, but it definitely has a point of view: a cool, gauzy vision of a mod, mod world.
But Leveaux's scattered production simmers when it should sizzle — it plays like a movie that needs another round of sharpening in the editing room.

The show now faces that all important Stage II of its life when the changing of the guard determines whether it can join the ranks of enduring hits which are rejuvenated rather than diminished by an ongoing parade of new actors.
This is not a show that can thrive on the merely competent staging Leveaux has given it; his work is unexceptional, unexciting, and mostly unmusical.

cn.t: A visually glamorous but thrill-free revival that doesn't escape the shadow of the original production. Critics find it respectable and elegant, though lacking magic and emotional depth.

vs.sum: The Eugene O'Neill Theatre offers decent sightlines, though some seats may have minor obstructions due to the shallow rake. Sound quality is generally good, ensuring an enjoyable auditory experience. While the comfort level is typical for Broadway, with standard legroom and seat width, the theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Georgian design. Facilities are adequate, with bars and merchandise available on both levels, though restroom capacity may be limited during peak times.

acc.note: No elevators. All accessible seating on Orchestra level. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops.
